name: Pixies
label: 4AD
lede: Black Francis wanted a bass player who liked Hüsker Dü and Peter, Paul and Mary, and Kim Deal answered the ad without owning a bass. Five records later he ended the band on the radio, and since 2004 they've been back for twice as long as they were gone.

eras.title: A letter from San Juan
eras.text: Two UMass Amherst students quit school over a letter from Puerto Rico and a shared taste for punk and David Bowie. In Boston they found a bass player through the classifieds and a drummer through her wedding.

years.src: Wikipedia: Joey Santiago · Wikipedia: Black Francis
years.h: Charles Thompson hears Joey Santiago through a dorm wall
years.p: At UMass Amherst, [[Joey Santiago|a51cfe50-b22b-4d01-8720-b3cacfeb3c58]] hears Charles Thompson playing guitar with his roommate, goes and gets his own guitar, and moves in with him the next semester.
years.xp: Thompson had started at UMass in 1983 to study anthropology. Santiago, born in Manila, had come to Longmeadow, Massachusetts as a boy, after his family left the Philippines in 1972 when Ferdinand Marcos declared martial law. The two bonded over punk and Bowie.

years.src: Wikipedia: Black Francis · Wikipedia: Joey Santiago · Wikipedia: Pixies
years.h: Six months in San Juan, and a letter home
years.p: Thompson spends six months in Puerto Rico on an exchange and writes to Santiago that it's time to start a band. Santiago says yes, and both leave school for Boston.
years.xp: The trip ran all through the early songs. A strange roommate in San Juan became 'Crackity Jones', and Puerto Rico turns up again in 'Vamos' and 'Isla de Encanta'.

years.cap: Black Francis, Kim Deal, Joey Santiago and David Lovering
years.h: Kim Deal answers a Boston Phoenix ad with no bass experience
years.p: Thompson's ad asks for a bass player into [[Hüsker Dü|5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06]] and Peter, Paul and Mary. [[Kim Deal|760e4df4-e851-46c8-b34d-afa2e9706831]] is the only one who answers, and she gets the job anyway.
years.xp:
The drummer came through Deal's husband, John Murphy, who had worked at a Radio Shack with David Lovering; Lovering met Deal at their wedding on Memorial Day 1985. He wasn't impressed by the band at first, then sat in and stayed.

Santiago picked the name by opening a dictionary at random: pixies, 'mischievous little elves'. By mid-1986 the band was rehearsing in Lovering's parents' garage.

eras.title: Albini, a bathroom and a flamenco dancer
eras.text: A demo paid for by Francis's father reached 4AD by way of a Walkman on a New York sidewalk. Then Steve Albini took $1,500 and no royalties, the British weeklies named the result album of the year, and the band's first big crowds were in England, opening for their Boston friends.

q: could not sleep until you guys are world famous
years.src: Wikipedia: Pixies · Wikipedia: Come On Pilgrim
years.h: The Purple Tape: 17 songs at Fort Apache
years.p: Producer Gary Smith catches the band on a bill with [[Throwing Muses|b1b9d5cc-7975-43e5-960e-670583da7bc8]] and records a 17-song demo at Fort Apache in Boston, paid for by Thompson's father. It comes in a purple cover.
years.xp: Promoter Ken Goes, who already managed a 4AD band, became the Pixies' manager and passed the tape to [[Ivo Watts-Russell|cf86cec1-1baf-4d8a-ba1e-01568332585a]]. Watts-Russell found it 'too rock 'n' roll' until his girlfriend Deborah Edgeley, a 4AD secretary, talked him round. Then he played it on his Walkman walking through New York and 'absolutely adored it from day one'.

years.src: Wikipedia: Come On Pilgrim · Wikipedia: Black Francis
years.h: Ivo Watts-Russell keeps eight songs and calls it Come On Pilgrim
years.p: 4AD's first Pixies record is the Purple Tape cut down to a mini-album, and the first time Thompson calls himself Black Francis, a name his father had been saving for another son.
years.xp: Watts-Russell chose eight of the 17 songs, saying there was 'too much that was just not that good'. He left off 'Here Comes Your Man' as 'too obviously commercial'. Vaughan Oliver designed the sleeve around a Simon Larbalestier photo of a man in a hair shirt.

years.src: Wikipedia: Surfer Rosa · Wikipedia: Where Is My Mind
years.h: Steve Albini moves Deal's vocals into the studio bathroom
years.p: At Q Division in Somerville, with ten working days booked, [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] wants more room on Deal's voice and takes the gear into a tiled bathroom.
years.xp:
Albini took a flat $1,500 fee and refused royalties, which he considered 'an insult to the band'. Sessions also ran at Downtown Recorders in Boston's South End, where 'Where Is My Mind?' was cut in November 1987.

The studio chatter he left on the record stayed there. 'It's on their record forever,' Albini said later, 'so I think now they are obliged to say that they're ok with it.'

years.src: Wikipedia: Surfer Rosa · Wikipedia: Where Is My Mind · Wikipedia: Pixies
years.h: Surfer Rosa is Melody Maker's album of the year
years.p: Thirteen songs in 33 minutes, with a Simon Larbalestier cover of a Portuguese flamenco dancer. Melody Maker and Sounds both name it the year's best; Rough Trade puts it out in the US in August.
years.xp:
'Where Is My Mind?' came from a UMass-era scuba dive in the Caribbean, where a tiny fish kept following Thompson around. Santiago called his guitar part 'a lazy arpeggio'.

The record went gold in the US in 2005. Pitchfork later gave it 10 out of 10.

years.h: The Pixies open for Throwing Muses on the 'Sex and Death' tour
years.p: The European run starts at the Mean Fiddler in London, with the Boston band as the support act.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kim Deal · Wikipedia: Surfer Rosa
years.h: Deal sings 'Gigantic' as Mrs. John Murphy
years.p: The only Pixies single with Deal on lead vocals, a song she co-wrote, reaches No. 93 in the UK. The credit is her joke.
years.xp: Deal called the name 'an ironic feminist joke', after talking with a woman who wanted to be known only by her husband's name. She used it on Come On Pilgrim and Surfer Rosa. She and John Murphy divorced the same year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Doolittle · Wikipedia: Here Comes Your Man
years.h: Francis hands Gil Norton a Buddy Holly record
years.p: Producer Gil Norton wants longer songs with more verses. Francis takes him to a record store, buys a Buddy Holly greatest hits, and points out that most of the songs are two or three minutes long.
years.xp: Recording ran October 31 to November 23, 1988 at Downtown Recorders in Boston, with mixing at Carriage House in Stamford, Connecticut. Norton won one argument: he championed 'Here Comes Your Man', which Francis was embarrassed by, and Francis 'threw him a bone'.

eras.title: A monkey goes to heaven
eras.text: Elektra took the Pixies to America, Gil Norton gave them a $40,000 budget, and Doolittle made them the band other bands talked about. On the road the four of them stopped talking to each other.

years.h: Doolittle puts a monkey with a halo in the Billboard 200
years.p: Four times the budget of Surfer Rosa, with Elektra handling America. It reaches No. 8 in the UK and No. 98 in the US, the band's first Billboard 200 entry, and later goes platinum.
years.xp: The cover is Larbalestier and Oliver again, with the numbers 5, 6 and 7 from 'Monkey Gone to Heaven', which came out first as a single on March 27 and made the Modern Rock top 10. Francis told Melody Maker the Old Testament characters in songs like 'Dead' and 'Gouge Away' were an obsession.

years.cap: Santiago, Black Francis, Lovering and Deal, 1989
years.h: Francis and Deal refuse to lip-sync 'Here Comes Your Man'
years.p: In the fish-eye video they hold their mouths wide open while the vocals play. Francis wrote the song at about 14; the single reaches No. 3 on the Modern Rock chart.

years.big: The tour was called 'Fuck or Fight'
years.h: Francis throws a guitar at Deal in Stuttgart
years.p: On the 'Fuck or Fight' tour after Doolittle, Deal nearly gets fired for refusing to play a show in Frankfurt.
years.xp: The band was exhausted. Santiago later said Deal was 'headstrong' and wanted to include her own songs. After the last date the four took time apart, and Deal went straight into a side project.

eras.title: California, U2 and a fax
eras.text: Three of the four moved to Los Angeles, Francis wrote everything, and the songs got stranger and louder. Two albums, a stadium tour with U2, and the band was over before most of America noticed it had started.

years.h: Deal makes Pod with The Breeders
years.p: With Throwing Muses' [[Tanya Donelly|478e2b34-bda3-48c8-81e4-77efac91f3ec]] and Albini recording in Edinburgh, [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]] release their first album. Deal stays in the UK for it while the others start Bossanova.

q: I was writing [lyrics] on napkins five minutes before I sang.
years.h: Pirate radio wrecks the Bossanova sessions
years.p: Everyone but Deal has moved to Los Angeles, 'because the recording studio was there', Lovering said. At Cherokee, pirate radio bleeds into the amps after 6 p.m., and Rick Rubin helps Norton move to Master Control in Burbank.

years.h: Twenty-three seconds of running, slowed down to fill 'Velouria'
years.p: For a Top of the Pops-eligible video, the band runs toward the camera in a quarry; the clip is stretched to the length of the song. 'Velouria' is their first UK Top 40 hit, at No. 28.
years.xp: 'We just ran towards it,' Santiago recalled. The director asked if that was all they had. 'Man, well, we'll just slow it down then.' The band didn't end up playing the song on the show.

years.cap: Ticket for the Pixies at the National Stadium, Dublin, October 1, 1990
years.h: Francis writes all of Bossanova, and Britain sends it to No. 3
years.p: Surf guitar and outer space. It reaches No. 70 in the US; 'Dig for Fire' follows in November.

years.h: Trompe le Monde is Deal's last Pixies album
years.p: Recorded in Burbank, Paris and London with [[Eric Drew Feldman|18bf31b2-1baf-438b-9b64-24c1f2a4eb7d]] on keyboards. 'U-Mass' uses a riff from their college days, and a cover of [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]]'s 'Head On' hits No. 6 on the Modern Rock chart.
years.xp: Deal's part shrank further. AllMusic's Heather Phares called the album 'essentially Black Francis' solo debut'.

years.cap: Deal, Santiago, Black Francis and Lovering
years.h: The Pixies open for U2 on the US Zoo TV Tour
years.p: A support slot on the US leg of the year's biggest tour, playing arenas to U2's crowds. It's the band's last run of shows for twelve years.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the last show before the breakup as the Commodore Ballroom in Vancouver.

years.big: Deal and Lovering found out by fax
years.src: Wikipedia: Pixies · Wikipedia: Black Francis · Magnet
years.h: Black Francis ends the Pixies on BBC Radio 5
years.p: He tells an interviewer the band is finished without telling the band first. Then he calls Santiago.
years.xp:
Tension between Francis and Deal had been building since Bossanova, when he began writing all the band's material. The split itself had happened in 1992; Radio 5 was where it went public.

The rest of the band got paper. "I just fucking sent a fax to the manager saying, 'Copy this fax and mail it to everyone. I'm fucking out of here,'" Francis told Magnet in 2014. "No confrontation, no discussion."

years.cap: Kim Deal with The Amps, Dayton, Ohio
years.src: Wikipedia: Black Francis · Wikipedia: Kim Deal · Wikipedia: Pixies
years.h: Frank Black goes solo on 4AD; The Breeders go platinum
years.p: Thompson flips his name to [[Frank Black|98a35a4d-a845-4282-bc7c-5679f2bb9bd2]] for a solo debut. Deal's Breeders put out Last Splash, with 'Cannonball', and it goes platinum.

eras.title: Cobain, Fight Club and a magician
eras.text: With the band gone, everybody else started explaining what it had meant. Nirvana said so in Rolling Stone, Fight Club said so with one song, and a drummer in a lab coat said so with physics.

years.big: I was basically trying to rip off the Pixies.
q: I should have been in that band.
years.src: Rolling Stone: Kurt Cobain · Wikipedia: Pixies
years.h: Kurt Cobain admits where 'Smells Like Teen Spirit' came from
years.p: Talking to Rolling Stone, Cobain says he was trying to write the ultimate pop song. He'd already picked Albini for In Utero because of Surfer Rosa.
years.xp:
"I was basically trying to rip off the Pixies. I have to admit it," Cobain told David Fricke. "When I heard the Pixies for the first time, I connected with that band so heavily I should have been in that band."

[[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] borrowed the quiet verse, loud chorus. Gary Smith said later that all sorts of bands ended up 'exploiting the same strategy of wide dynamics'.

years.src: Wikipedia: David Lovering · Wikipedia: Joey Santiago
years.h: Lovering becomes the Scientific Phenomenalist
years.p: Broke after the split, the drummer takes up magic after a convention trip with Grant-Lee Phillips, doing physics experiments on stage in a lab coat. He drums for Cracker and Nitzer Ebb, and turns down the [[Foo Fighters|67f66c07-6e61-4026-ade5-7e782fad3a5d]].
years.xp: 'I couldn't top the Pixies,' Lovering said of why he switched to magic. He had trained in electronic engineering at Wentworth and built lasers before the band. Santiago, meanwhile, started the Martinis with his wife Linda Mallari and wrote music for film and TV, including Undeclared.

years.src: Wikipedia: Where Is My Mind · Wikipedia: Pixies
years.h: Fight Club ends on 'Where Is My Mind?'
years.p: David Fincher plays the Surfer Rosa song over the buildings coming down. It becomes the band's best-known song for a generation that never saw them.

eras.title: Sold out in minutes
eras.text: Some phone calls in 2003 turned into quiet rehearsals, and a tour announced in February 2004 sold out in minutes. The four of them played the old songs better than ever and still didn't say much to each other offstage.

years.cap: The reunion tour at the Uptown Theatre, Kansas City, October 1, 2004
years.src: Wikipedia: Pixies · Wikipedia: Black Francis · Wikipedia: Bam Thwok
years.h: The Pixies play the Fine Line in Minneapolis, twelve years on
years.p: The first show of the reunion, a club warm-up before Coachella and a world tour that grossed over $14 million.
years.xp:
The European leg ran from Reykjavík on May 26 to Chelmsford on August 22. In June the band put out a new Kim Deal song, 'Bam Thwok', on the iTunes Music Store, where it hit No. 1 on the UK download chart.

DreamWorks had asked for a song for Shrek 2's title sequence, then turned it down. Francis called the session "a nice way to break the ice."

years.h: loudQUIETloud films the reunion
years.p: Steven Cantor and Matthew Galkin's documentary follows the 2004 tour, including Lovering's father dying midway through and Lovering drinking hard after. Thompson said the editing made it look worse than it was.

eras.title: Life after Kim
eras.text: Deal left during the first new sessions in two decades, and the bass chair turned over three times in eleven years. The records kept coming anyway: five albums since 2014.

years.src: Magnet · Wikipedia: Pixies · Wikipedia: Kim Deal
years.h: Kim Deal leaves, and 'Bagboy' comes out the same month
years.p: She'd walked out of the first new sessions in two decades, at a studio in Wales with Gil Norton, in fall 2012. The first new song, given away free, has vocals from Jeremy Dubs.
years.xp:
Francis says Deal walked into the café while he and Santiago were having their espresso, ordered a cappuccino and said: "I'm flying home tomorrow." He and Santiago left for the bar. She called Francis from the airport as she boarded.

"We never got to the bottom of it," he told Magnet.

years.src: Guardian: Bassist Kim Shattuck · Magnet · Wikipedia: Kim Shattuck
years.h: Kim Shattuck is out after one European tour
years.p: The morning after the band said goodbye at the airport, the manager called The Muffs' singer: they were going with another bass player. She'd been in since July 1.
years.xp:
Shattuck wondered about a show at the Mayan in Los Angeles where she jumped into the crowd. The manager told her not to do it again, she said; not for her safety, "No, because the Pixies don't do that."

Francis told Magnet it was personality as much as playing: "She's very West Coast, she's very extrovert. We're very East Coast, very introvert."

Shattuck died on October 2, 2019, at 56, of complications from ALS. She had never made the diagnosis public.

years.cap: Paz Lenchantin on bass with the Pixies
years.h: Paz Lenchantin, a 'die-hard' fan, takes the bass
years.p: The ex-A Perfect Circle and [[Zwan|5af2629b-36de-486c-ad50-a89a28ff050f]] bassist joins for the 2014 tour and becomes a full member in July 2016.

years.cap: Santiago, Black Francis and Lovering at Huxleys Neue Welt, Berlin
years.h: Indie Cindy, the first Pixies album in 23 years
years.p: Three EPs released between September 2013 and March 2014, collected as one album.

years.h: Head Carrier gives Lenchantin a lead vocal
years.p: 'All I Think About Now' is her first lead on a Pixies record.

years.h: Beneath the Eyrie, with a podcast about making it
years.p: The band documents the recording in 'It's a Pixies Podcast'. Lenchantin sings 'Los Surfers Muertos'.

years.h: Doggerel on BMG
years.p: The band's eighth album, led by 'There's a Moon On', following the stand-alone single 'Human Crime' in March.

years.cap: Emma Richardson and David Lovering at Victorious Festival, August 2024
years.h: Lenchantin leaves, and says it wasn't her choice
years.p: The band says she's going to concentrate on her own projects. She tells Rolling Stone it was 'a bit of a surprise' to her too. Emma Richardson of Band of Skulls takes over.

years.h: The Night the Zombies Came, and almost no zombies
years.p: Produced by Tom Dalgety, with Richardson's first studio credit on 'You're So Impatient'.
years.xp: Francis on the title: 'It's not like I wrote a bunch of songs about zombies.' The other lyrics, he said, 'just sounded corny as shit' as titles.
